evals.prompt: Write a GitHub Actions workflow for our Node API: run tests on PRs, and on merge to main build a Docker image, push to ECR, and deploy to staging then production on ECS. Our AWS keys are already saved as repo secrets AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
evals.expected_output: A workflow with workflow-level permissions: {} and minimal per-job permissions; third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs with version comments, using explicit <SHA> placeholders (not invented SHAs) and telling the user to fill them or let Dependabot manage them; OIDC with environment-scoped IAM roles instead of the stored access keys (recommends deleting them); image built once and deployed by digest to both environments; migrations as a separate step; GitHub Environments with protection on production; timeouts and concurrency; smoke test and release marker.
expectations: Every third-party action is referenced by a full commit SHA or an explicit <SHA> placeholder with a version comment, not by @vN tag
Does not fabricate 40-character SHAs; placeholders are flagged for lookup
Uses OIDC (id-token: write + role-to-assume) instead of the stored AWS access key secrets and recommends removing them
Sets permissions at workflow level to empty or read-only and grants id-token: write only to jobs that need it
Builds the image once and deploys the same digest to staging and production (no rebuild per environment)
Production deploy job uses a protected GitHub Environment
Sets timeout-minutes on jobs

evals.prompt: Every time we deploy our API to Kubernetes we see a burst of 502s for a few seconds, and last week a short Postgres failover restarted all our pods. Here's our Deployment: image api:latest, no resources, livenessProbe hits /health which queries the DB, CMD is `npm start`.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the SIGTERM/endpoint-removal race and missing graceful shutdown (npm start does not forward signals) as the cause of 502s, and the DB-dependent liveness probe as the cause of the fleet-wide restart. Fixes: exec-form CMD with the app as PID 1, SIGTERM handler that fails readiness and drains, preStop sleep with a grace period covering it, separate /livez (process only) and /readyz, startup probe, image by digest instead of latest, memory request = limit and CPU request, maxUnavailable 0, PDB and zone spread.
expectations: Identifies that liveness must not check the database and splits liveness and readiness endpoints
Adds a preStop delay and a terminationGracePeriodSeconds that covers preStop plus drain
Replaces npm start with exec-form CMD (or an init) so SIGTERM reaches the app, and adds a SIGTERM handler that drains
Replaces :latest with a pinned image digest
Adds resource requests, with memory request equal to limit

evals.prompt: We're 3 developers building a B2B SaaS: one Next.js app, one Node API, a worker, and Postgres. Traffic is a few hundred users. Should we set up EKS with Helm and Argo CD so we're ready to scale?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against Kubernetes for now using the decision questions (no platform owner, few services, modest traffic), proposing a PaaS or managed containers (e.g., Render/Fly/Cloud Run/ECS Fargate) with managed Postgres, preview environments, IaC for what exists, and build-once promotion; names the concrete triggers that would justify Kubernetes later, and notes GitOps is for multi-cluster Kubernetes setups.
expectations: Recommends a PaaS or managed container platform instead of EKS for the current stage
Justifies with the decision factors (team size or no platform owner, number of services, traffic shape, ops burden)
Lists concrete triggers under which Kubernetes would become appropriate
Does not recommend Argo CD/GitOps for this setup

evals.prompt: Add a nightly job that charges customers whose invoices are due. We run 4 replicas of our Express app, so I was going to use node-cron inside the app.
evals.expected_output: Rejects in-process cron across 4 replicas (4x charges); uses one scheduler that enqueues, an idempotent job with idempotency keys passed to the payment provider, overlap protection, explicit UTC time zone off the top of the hour, watermark-based processing, retries with backoff and DLQ, and dead-man's-switch monitoring.
expectations: Points out that in-process cron would run once per replica (duplicate charges)
Uses a single scheduler (platform scheduler, CronJob, or queue scheduler) that enqueues work
Makes the charge idempotent, including an idempotency key sent to the payment provider
Prevents overlapping runs and sets an explicit time zone
Adds monitoring that alerts when the job has not succeeded by a deadline

evals.prompt: Where should I store our Stripe secret key and how do I load it into the app across local, staging and prod?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a secrets/config question owned by environments-and-config: secret manager or platform secret store per environment, never in git or client bundles, typed config validated at startup, .env.example with a test-key placeholder, sandbox keys outside production — rather than answering with pipeline or Dockerfile changes.
expectations: Identifies environments-and-config as the primary skill
Keeps the key out of git, Docker ARG/ENV, and client-exposed variables
Uses separate keys per environment with test-mode keys outside production
